bottleneck: BCIs record the most intimate data that exists — intentions, emotions, covert speech — yet neural data privacy law is nascent. Colorado's 2024 neural-data legislation and proposed EU amendments are early exceptions; most jurisdictions have no rules on who owns brain recordings, what inferences may be drawn from them, or how long they may be stored. Commercial incentives push toward exactly the profiling and manipulation these data enable, and once neural data leaks, it cannot be changed like a password.
current_state: Regulation is fragmented and mostly prospective. Consumer EEG products already collect neural data under standard, weak privacy terms that few users read.

sources.title: Over 200 Brain-Computer Interface Companies Established, Yet Experts Highlight Key Challenges

title: Neural data privacy law lags BCI deployment
why_it_blocks: Without cognitive-liberty protections, BCIs risk becoming surveillance devices worn inside the skull. Public trust — and adoption — depends on rules that do not yet exist, and a single scandal could set the field back years.
